direct_answer:
As of December 31, 2024, BASF’s own workforce comprised 111,822 employees: 81,572 men and 30,250 women (0 not disclosed) [Source 2]. By employment/contract type and gender (as of December 31, 2024): permanent employees 106,776 (78,081 men; 28,695 women); temporary employees 2,105 (1,183 men; 922 women); apprentices 2,941 (2,308 men; 633 women); non-guaranteed hours employees 0 (0 men; 0 women) [Source 3].

Women held 29.3% of leadership positions with disciplinary responsibility worldwide as of December 31, 2024 [Source 1].
compliance_rationale: The passages provide a clear breakdown of total employees by gender and by contract/employment type (permanent, temporary, apprentices, and non-guaranteed hours) as of a point-in-time (Dec 31, 2024) [Source 2][Source 3]. They also provide the percentage of women in leadership positions with disciplinary responsibility (29.3%), which supports the requested percentage of management positions held by women [Source 1]. However, the required ESRS S1-6 methodological details (e.g., headcount vs FTE, point-in-time vs average explicitly, and cross-reference to the most representative number in the financial statements) are only partially evidenced in the provided excerpts [Source 8][Source 12]. Additionally, ESRS S1-9 asks for gender distribution at top management level in number and percentage; only a percentage for leadership positions is provided, without numbers and without explicit confirmation it is 'top management' as defined by ESRS [Source 1].
disclosure_gaps: Explicit methodological statement whether employee figures are headcount or FTE (not evidenced in provided passages).
Clarification whether the employee numbers are point-in-time or average over the reporting period (the date is given, but methodology is not explicitly stated as required).
Cross-reference to the most representative employee number in the financial statements (only a general reference to where wage and salary expenses are reported is provided) [Source 8].
Any assumptions/context used in compiling workforce composition figures (not evidenced in provided passages).
ESRS S1-9: number of women and men at top management level (only a percentage for leadership positions with disciplinary responsibility is provided) [Source 1].
ESRS S1-9: explicit statement that the disclosed leadership metric corresponds to 'top management level' as defined by ESRS (not evidenced in provided passages).
key_findings: Total employees as of Dec 31, 2024: 111,822; men 81,572; women 30,250 [Source 2].
Women in leadership positions with disciplinary responsibility worldwide: 29.3% as of Dec 31, 2024 [Source 1].
